title: Reported Speech Gap-Fill Quiz
note: One file for the whole topic: the rules page, the practice page and the quiz all read this, so a correction lands everywhere at once.

examples.after: They <<said>> (that) they <<were going>> to the cinema.
Tom <<said>> (that) he <<couldn't>> come the next day.

sets.setTitle: Set 2: Tell + Person - Direct Object Required

examples.after: They <<told us>> (that) they <<had>> a new car.
He <<told her>> (that) the meeting <<had been>> cancelled.
John <<told me>> (that) he <<had seen>> my brother the day before.
She said (that) she would see me <<the next day>>.
Tom said (that) he had met him <<the day before>>.
They said (that) they were leaving <<that night>>.
He said (that) he would do it <<then>>.

examples.before: "<<Are>> you coming to the party?" she <<asked>>.
examples.after: She <<asked>> (me) <<if/whether>> I <<was>> coming to the party.

sets.setTitle: Set 2: Wh- Questions - Keep Question Word

examples.before: "Can you help me?" he <<wanted to know>>.
examples.after: He <<wanted to know>> <<if/whether>> I <<could>> help him.

examples.before: "<<Close>> the door!" she said to me.
examples.after: She <<told me to close>> the door.

examples.before: "<<Don't be>> late!" he said to them.
examples.after: He <<told them not to be>> late.

examples.before: "<<Finish>> your homework," the teacher said to us.
examples.after: The teacher <<told us to finish>> our homework.

examples.before: "<<Don't touch>> that!" she said to him.
examples.after: She <<told him not to touch>> that.

examples.before: "<<Wait>> here," the officer said to me.
examples.after: The officer <<told me to wait>> there.

examples.before: "Could you <<open>> the window?" he said to me.
examples.after: He <<asked me to open>> the window.

examples.before: "Please <<don't tell>> anyone," she said to us.
examples.after: She <<asked us not to tell>> anyone.

examples.before: "Would you <<call>> me later?" Tom said to her.
examples.after: Tom <<asked her to call>> him later.

examples.before: "Please <<be>> quiet," the librarian said to them.
examples.after: The librarian <<asked them to be>> quiet.

examples.before: "<<Stay>> where you are!" the police officer said.
examples.after: The police officer <<ordered>> us <<to stay>> where we were.

examples.before: "<<Don't touch>> the wire," he said to me.
examples.after: He <<warned me not to touch>> the wire.

examples.before: "You should <<see>> a doctor," she said to him.
examples.after: She <<advised him to see>> a doctor.

examples.before: "<<Don't forget>> to lock the door," she said to me.
examples.after: She <<reminded me to lock>> the door.

examples.before: "<<Leave>> immediately!" the manager said to them.
examples.after: The manager <<ordered them to leave>> immediately.
He <<admitted breaking>> the window. / He <<admitted (that)>> he <<had broken>> the window.
She <<denied taking>> my money. / She <<denied (that)>> she <<had taken>> my money.
Tom <<admitted making>> a mistake. / Tom <<admitted (that)>> he <<had made>> a mistake.
He <<denied stealing>> the car. / He <<denied (that)>> he <<had stolen>> the car.
She <<admitted lying>> to me. / She <<admitted (that)>> she <<had lied>> to me.

examples.before: "Why don't we <<go>> to the cinema?" she said.
examples.after: She <<suggested going>> to the cinema. / She <<suggested (that)>> we <<(should) go>> to the cinema.
Tom <<suggested having>> a break. / Tom <<suggested (that)>> we <<(should) have>> a break.
She <<suggested meeting>> the next day. / She <<suggested (that)>> we <<(should) meet>> the next day.

examples.before: "You should <<see>> a doctor," he said to me.
examples.after: He <<suggested seeing>> a doctor. / He <<suggested (that)>> I <<(should) see>> a doctor.
They <<suggested leaving>> early. / They <<suggested (that)>> we <<(should) leave>> early.

examples.before: "I really must <<pay>> for the meal," she said.
examples.after: She <<insisted on paying>> for the meal. / She <<insisted (that)>> she <<pay/should pay>> for the meal.

examples.before: "You absolutely have to <<come>> with us," they said.
examples.after: They <<insisted on>> us <<coming>> with them. / They <<insisted (that)>> we <<come/should come>> with them.
He <<insisted on helping>> me. / He <<insisted (that)>> he <<help/should help>> me.

examples.before: "You must <<take>> the money," she said to me.
examples.after: She <<insisted on>> my <<taking>> the money. / She <<insisted (that)>> I <<take/should take>> the money.

examples.before: "I won't <<leave>> until you apologize," Tom said.
examples.after: Tom <<insisted on>> not <<leaving>> until I apologized. / Tom <<insisted (that)>> he <<wouldn't leave>> until I apologized.

examples.before: "I <<will punish>> you if you do that again," Dad said.
examples.after: Dad <<threatened to punish>> me if I did that again.

examples.before: "I <<will definitely finish>> it tomorrow," Tom said.
examples.after: Tom <<promised to finish>> it the next day.

sets.setTitle: Set 2: Offer, Refuse, Agree + To + Infinitive

examples.before: "I'll <<carry>> your bags," he said to me.
"Shall I <<help>> you?" she said to me.
"No, I won't <<sign>> the contract," he said.

sets.setTitle: Set 3: Accuse, Congratulate, Apologize + For/On + Gerund

examples.before: "You <<stole>> my pen!" she said to him.
examples.after: She <<accused him of stealing>> her pen.

examples.before: "Well done on <<passing>> your exam!" he said to me.
examples.after: He <<congratulated me on passing>> my exam.

examples.before: "I'm sorry I <<broke>> your vase," she said.
"You <<cheated>> in the test," the teacher said to Tom.
examples.after: The teacher <<accused Tom of cheating>> in the test.
Tom <<told her (that)>> he <<would call>> her the next day.
She <<asked (me) if/whether>> I <<had seen>> her keys.
He <<said (that)>> the train <<had left>> an hour before.

examples.before: "<<Close>> the door!" she said to me.
examples.after: She <<told me to close>> the door.
He <<admitted taking/admitted (that) he had taken>> my phone.
Tom <<denied breaking/denied (that) he had broken>> the window.
They <<insisted on>> us <<coming/insisted (that) we come>> with them.

examples.before: "<<Don't touch>> the wire!" he said to me.
examples.after: He <<warned me not to touch>> the wire.

examples.before: "Well done on <<winning>>!" they said to her.

"I lost my keys yesterday," said Pedro.

examples.original: "We'll call you tomorrow," they said.
examples.before: They said they would call me

"I'm working here this week," Maria told me.
